Senses.Explanation: Literally, to raise up and make prominent. The expression occurs 1,627 times in 275 allowlisted texts. Chan records make it a public teaching-seat verb: a master proclaims the sect's purport, presents 'this matter' before the assembly, or is asked in an interview to present a cited event. One opening discourse pairs opening the hall with 'proclaiming the teaching of the school'; another records a whisk transmitted with the charge to present this matter before the human and heavenly assembly. A later discourse says that one sentence had already been presented before the listeners entered the gate.
Senses.Note: No definition formula was found. The deviation is institutional and observable: the ordinary verb becomes a recurrent description of a master's public work from the teaching seat. The corpus does not support separate senses for different subjects raised; all are objects of the same transitive act.

Occurrences.Kwic: 爍破重關，徹法源底，逼得山僧無藏隱處，今日不免對眾舉揚。煩維那宣讀。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yinyuan (隱元禪師語錄), Yinyuan Longqi's Huangbo Mountain record. Yinyuan Longqi holds up the invitation, says it has forced him from concealment so that today he cannot avoid raising and proclaiming the matter before the assembly, and asks the rector to read it aloud. Huangbo here names the mountain and monastery, not Huangbo Xiyun.

Occurrences.Kwic: 為國開堂，舉揚宗教，山僧不敢囊藏被葢
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 列祖提綱錄, Yuanwu Keqin's imperial-command opening of Chongning Monastery. Yuanwu Keqin is the exact speaker: he says that in opening the hall for the country he raises the lineage teaching and will not conceal what buddhas cannot exhaust and patriarchs cannot lift.

Occurrences.Kwic: 擲鉢峰前事，請師為舉揚。師云：風不來，樹不動。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 建中靖國續燈錄, Ciming Chuyuan section. The exact headword-bearing speaker is an unnamed questioning monk who asks Ciming to raise and proclaim the matter before Zhibo Peak. All six rungs leave him unnamed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 諸人未入門時，一句子已向汝舉揚了也，更待興問酬荅
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 百癡禪師語錄, requested hall address. Baichi Yuan is the exact speaker: after the opening verse he tells the assembly that before they entered the gate a phrase had already been raised and displayed to them.

Occurrences.Kwic: 付與山僧，曰：『向後人天眾前舉揚個事去。』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 石雨禪師法檀, Shiyu Mingfang's hall address quoting his late teacher. Zhanran Yuancheng is the exact speaker of the stored command: Shiyu says his late teacher, the Yunmen master Zhanran, handed him the worn fly-whisk and told him to raise and proclaim the matter before human and celestial assemblies.
